I think in practice this is only used for timing information so we should probably have some notes that timing information can be misleading for full duplex implementations. body:
Fair enough, thanks for the clarification.

Thinking about this again, in the full duplex mode, aren't those phases the same as well?
`responding` is after the response is handed over to the caller, it doesn't necessarily mean you can't keep pumping data into the request stream, and `concluded` is once both the request and response are done (streams are closed).

body:
No, I think the older terms were better. Fetching encompasses both.

The problem is that "responding" might finish while "requesting" is still ongoing. There's no good way to represent that unless we go with a bit field of sorts.

I think the best we can do for now is call out the limitations of this representation in a note and be very careful with what we build on top of it.

body:
Yes, that's the idea of `initiatorType`. You want to know where the request came from, not which kind of request it is (which `destination` already covers). That's why e.g. a CSS image request would have a destination `image` and an initiator `css`.

 I do agree that `initiatorType` is a bit inconsistent, and there are several open issues like https://github.com/w3c/resource-timing/issues/132 to address this. But I want the spec to catch up with implementations before we get to it.
